text:
sam: Quick heads-up — scheduled runtime patch for GPU kernels tonight 03/29 00:00-03:00 UTC. Expected impact: short Dedicated pin to older runtime for a few customers, and transient throttling while nodes recycle. Need a customer-facing statuspage snippet + an email blurb.
jordan: ack. Is this a forced pin for any committed Dedicated pools or just transient routing fallback?
maya: It'll be a transient pin for any in-flight workloads hitting the newer kernel. We plan automatic fallback to the previous pinned runtime for affected customers. No model data migration.
release-bot: Deploy scheduled by @maya -> runtime-gpu-kernel-2026-03-29-00 on cluster-us-west-2. Canary window 00:00-00:30 UTC. Auto-rollback threshold: 5% error increase OR latency >200ms p95 for 10m.
sam: good. Jordan, can you draft statuspage snippet? Keep it short and neutral. Ops will send targeted emails to customers with pinned capacity the minute we detect routing to fallback.
jordan: draft below — please sanity-check.
jordan: ```Status: Under Maintenance
Component: Redwood Dedicated inference runtime (GPU kernel patch)
Start: 2026-03-29 00:00 UTC
End: 2026-03-29 03:00 UTC (estimated)
Impact: Brief automated fallback to previous runtime for a subset of Dedicated customers; minimal request throttling possible. No customer data changes.
Notes: We will update this page when all regions return to normal.``` 
maya: looks good. Add a single-line note: "If you have strict pinning requirements, reply to this thread and we’ll coordinate a no-roll change window." That helps enterprise customers.
jordan: added.
sam: now email/snippet for targeted notify to customers with pinned capacity. Keep action-oriented.
lee: here's a compact email draft — can someone confirm tone?
lee: ```Subject: Planned maintenance: brief runtime patch (03/29 00:00 UTC)

Hi <CustomerName>,

We’re applying a brief maintenance patch to the Redwood Dedicated runtime on 2026-03-29 00:00–03:00 UTC. During the window some Dedicated pools may be automatically routed to a temporarily pinned runtime version to ensure request stability. You might see short bursts of throttling (seconds to minutes) while routing completes.

If your workloads require uninterrupted pinned versions, please reply to this message or contact your CSM and we’ll schedule a dedicated change window.

We’ll post updates to the status page and follow up after the maintenance completes.

Thanks,
Redwood Support Team``` 
maya: prefer to include a link placeholder to the status page and a contact alias. Replace CSM with support@redwood.ai for general customers.
lee: updated draft with link and alias.
opsbot: Canary monitor: canary-01 latency p95 = 145ms (baseline 120ms), errors 0.2% (baseline 0.1%). All within thresholds.
sam: if canary breaches auto-rollback thresholds, ops will trigger a rollback and we’ll push an updated status note. Confirm rollback playbook is ready?
maya: rollback playbook is ready. Steps: 1) hold further rollout, 2) revert routing to previous runtime variant, 3) run smoke tests for 10m, 4) notify customers via status page and targeted email. I’ve uploaded the smoke test checklist to the runbook.
jordan: ok to post statuspage now? opsbot is green.
sam: yes. Post the statuspage snippet and queue the email template for customers with pinned pools. Use batch send only after a routing fallback is observed for a customer to avoid false alarms.
release-bot: Canary window ended. Canary results: pass. Proceeding with staged rollout.
opsbot: Stage-1 rollout started in us-west-2. Monitoring group alpha.
lee: queued emails for 12 customers that have explicit Dedicated pins (will only send if we detect fallback). Template ready.
opsbot: Stage-1 metrics t+10m: latency p95 = 130ms, errors 0.08% — stable.
sam: great. Keep this thread for status updates and paste the final post-maint debrief here once complete. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
